evals.prompt: I want to deploy the audio-analyzer microservice on a machine with an Intel GPU. I don't want to rebuild from source, just pull the published image. Walk me through the exact steps, the env vars I need, and how to confirm the GPU is actually being used after startup.
evals.expected_output: A Docker Compose deployment walkthrough grounded in this service's actual compose file, env vars, and device passthrough behavior.
expectations: Uses docker compose pull followed by docker compose up -d rather than build.
Mentions REGISTRY and RELEASE_TAG in .env.
States that /dev/dri is passed through by default for GPU and no extra ACCEL_MOUNT_PATH is needed for GPU-only.
Shows checking ov.Core().available_devices inside the container to confirm GPU visibility.
Uses port 8010 and curl http://127.0.0.1:8010/health to verify health.

evals.prompt: The container starts and /health is fine, but inside the container openvino.Core().available_devices only shows CPU even though I set ACCEL_MOUNT_PATH to /dev/accel/accel0 in my .env before starting. Give me a focused debug sequence specific to this service, not generic Docker advice.
evals.expected_output: An NPU-specific debug checklist grounded in this service's Compose device mapping and known failure modes.
expectations: Recommends docker compose config to check the resolved services.audio-analyzer.devices mapping.
Recommends ls -l /dev/accel/ on the host and inside the container to confirm the node exists.
Mentions ZE_ENABLE_ALT_DRIVERS=libze_intel_npu.so must remain set in the container environment.
Mentions RENDER_GID / host render group access as a possible cause.
Notes that .env changes require the container to have been started (or restarted) after the variable was set, not just present in .env.

evals.prompt: I configured models.asr.name: whisper-large with provider openvino and device NPU, and it fails during or right after startup with something about pfnAppendGraphExecute. Is this an audio-analyzer bug I should try to patch around, and what should I actually do?
evals.expected_output: An accurate explanation that this is a known NPU driver/firmware inference limitation for whisper-large, not an application bug, with a concrete recommended fix.
expectations: States this is a confirmed NPU driver/firmware limitation, not an audio-analyzer defect.
Explains that whisper-large compiles but fails at inference time on NPU.
States that whisper-tiny/base/small/medium are validated to work on NPU.
Recommends switching whisper-large to CPU or GPU instead of trying to patch code.
Does not suggest disabling OpenVINO validation or bypassing the startup check as a fix.

evals.prompt: I want to turn on speaker diarization for my deployment. What do I need to set up, and what happens if I get the Hugging Face token or license acceptance wrong — does the whole service go down?
evals.expected_output: A diarization setup guide that correctly describes the soft-fail behavior when credentials are missing or incomplete.
expectations: Mentions setting models.asr.diarization: true in config.yaml.
Mentions obtaining an HF token and accepting the Pyannote speaker-diarization model license as a one-time gate.
Explains HF_TOKEN must be set (env or .env) before starting the service.
States clearly that missing/invalid credentials cause a warning and diarization is disabled for that session, not a service crash.
Distinguishes this from a hard startup validation failure (e.g. invalid provider/device).

evals.prompt: After a host reboot and some volume cleanup, the container now fails with PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied on /app/audio_analyzer/storage/... What's actually going on and how do I fix it without just chmod -R 777'ing things?
evals.expected_output: A grounded explanation of the UID/GID 1000:1000 ownership model and the correct volume-reset remedy.
expectations: Explains the container always runs as UID/GID 1000:1000, baked into the image.
Explains named volumes are initialized with that ownership on a fresh run, and the error usually means a volume was created by an earlier root-only run.
Recommends docker compose down followed by removing the specific named volumes and docker compose up -d again.
Warns that removing the volumes deletes cached models and session data, and to confirm before doing it.
Does not recommend chmod 777 or changing the user: directive in docker-compose.yml as the fix.

evals.prompt: I need to run the audio-analyzer test suite in CI without any GPU, Docker daemon, or downloaded model weights available. Which tests should I run and how do I invoke just those?
evals.expected_output: A CI-safe test invocation that correctly distinguishes this project's two test suites and uses the right marker/path for each.
expectations: Identifies that this codebase has two test suites: the unmarked root-level tests/*.py and the tier-marked tests/functional/ suite.
States tier1 is CI-safe: no model weights, no Docker, no GPU required.
Shows a command that targets tests/functional with -m tier1 (e.g. pytest tests/functional -v -m tier1), not a bare pytest with no path.
Explains that tier2 needs HF_TOKEN and tier3 needs a Docker daemon or live server, and why those are unsuitable for the stated CI constraint.
Does not recommend running the full suite unfiltered, and does not claim a bare `pytest -m tier1` with no path argument would find the functional tests.

evals.prompt: I want to run the streaming and VSS endpoint tests for audio-analyzer, but when I add -m tier1 to the pytest command nothing gets collected. What am I doing wrong?
evals.expected_output: A correct explanation that these particular tests belong to the unmarked root-level suite and must be run without any -m filter.
expectations: Identifies tests/test_streaming_endpoints.py and tests/test_vss_endpoints.py as part of the root-level suite that has no tier1/tier2/tier3 markers at all.
Explains that adding -m tier1 excludes every test in this suite because none of them carry that marker.
Gives the correct invocation without a -m filter, e.g. pytest tests/test_streaming_endpoints.py tests/test_vss_endpoints.py -v.
States these tests require no model weights or GPU.
Distinguishes this suite from the separate tier-marked tests/functional/ suite.

evals.prompt: Before deploying a Dockerfile change for audio-analyzer, I want to verify the image actually builds and that the NPU device mapping in docker-compose.yml still resolves correctly, without standing up the full service. What's the right test to run?
evals.expected_output: A correct pointer to the Tier-3 Docker build verification suite and an accurate description of what it checks.
expectations: Points to tests/functional/build/test_build.py and the command pytest tests/functional/build/test_build.py -m tier3 -v -s.
States this suite runs real docker compose build --no-cache against a live Docker daemon, not mocked.
Mentions it verifies the built image appears in the local Docker image store using the image name read from docker-compose.yml.
Mentions it verifies the ACCEL_MOUNT_PATH to /dev/accel/accel0 device mapping resolves correctly, including the /dev/null fallback when unset.
Notes that tests in this file skip (not fail) when no Docker daemon is reachable.

evals.prompt: A teammate says transcription on our audio-analyzer deployment feels slower than before, but we aren't sure if that's real or just their network. Is there a way to check the actual last-call latency and confirm which model/device is active without digging through container logs?
evals.expected_output: A correct pointer to the service's undocumented debug endpoints for model introspection and latency.
expectations: References GET /v1/model-info to confirm the active model, provider, device, and weight_format.
References GET /v1/performance to retrieve the last ASR call's latency in milliseconds.
Notes that /v1/performance reports only the most recent call's latency, not a rolling history or average.
Notes these endpoints are not part of the published OpenAI-compatible API reference but exist in api/custom_endpoints.py.
Uses port 8010 in any example given.
